## Why This Is Asked
Tests building robust, scalable guardrails across AKS namespaces, Azure Policy, and secret management; includes canary rollouts and UEBA-driven rollback for real production risk.

## Key Concepts
- AKS per-namespace policies and identity management
- Azure Policy gates for prod guardrails
- Managed identities for Key Vault access with short-lived creds
- Secret rotation and no secrets embedded in code
- Canary deployments with feature flags
- UEBA/Azure Sentinel for automated remediation

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kubernetes NetworkPolicy (simplified)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-public-egress
  namespace: prod
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
```

```json
{
  "policyName": "AKS-prod-allow-keyvault",

    "scope": "/subscriptions/xxx/resourceGroups/rg-prod",
    "parameters": {}
  }
}
```

- What telemetry would drive the UEBA-driven rollback and how would you implement it?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests network isolation basics and a practical rollback path in Azure.

## Key Concepts

- Azure Private Link / Private Endpoint
- Azure Policy to deny public network access
- Private DNS zones
- Rollout with canary, rollback plan
- Observability and testing

## Code Example

```javascript
# Create a resource group
az group create -n rg-secure -l eastus

# Create a virtual network
az network vnet create -g rg-secure -n vnet-sec -l eastus --address-prefix 10.0.0.0/16 --subnet-name priv -a 10.0.0.0/24

# Private Endpoint for Azure SQL
az network private-endpoint create -g rg-secure -n pe-sql -l eastus --vnet-name vnet-sec --subnet priv \
  --private-connection-resource-id $(az sql server show -g rg-sql -n myserver --query id -o tsv) \
  --private-connection-name sql-pe

# Private Endpoint for Databricks
az network private-endpoint create -g rg-secure -n pe-databr -l eastus --vnet-name vnet-sec --subnet priv \
  --private-connection-resource-id $(az databricks workspace show -g rg-db -n mydbx --query id -o tsv) \
  --private-connection-name dbx-pe

# Policy: deny public network access
az policy definition create -n Deny-Public-Network-Access --policy-definition '{
  \"if\": {
    \"anyOf\": [
      {\"field\": \"type\", \"equals\": \"Microsoft.Sql/servers\"},
      {\"field\": \"type\", \"equals\": \"Microsoft.Databricks/workspaces\"}
    ]
  },
  \"then\": {\"effect\": \"deny\"}
}'

az policy assignment create -n Deny-Public-Network-Access -d \"Deny public network access for SQL and Databricks\" -p /subscriptions/<sub>/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions/Deny-Public-Network-Access
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical design of a privacy-preserving telemetry workflow in Azure, focusing on data governance, tenant isolation, and safe rollback controls.

## Key Concepts

- Azure Purview for automated data classification
- Per-tenant isolation strategies in Data Lake Storage
- Customer-managed keys (CMK) in Azure Key Vault
- Managed Identities for secure service-to-service authentication
- Azure Policy to prevent secrets from being embedded in configurations
- Canary deployments with feature flags via Azure App Configuration
- End-to-end monitoring with Azure Monitor and incident response through Microsoft Sentinel

## Code Example

```bash
# Enable a canary flag and route 5% traffic
az appconfig feature set --key telemetry.canary.enabled --label production --value true
az appconfig feature set --key telemetry.canary.percentage --label production --value 5
```

This approach ensures complete data isolation between tenants while maintaining flexibility for policy changes and comprehensive observability.
